label: Institution
name: Catholic Orthodox Church of France
summary:
The Catholic Orthodox Church of France (French: Église Catholique Orthodoxe de France, ECOF) was a significant 20th-century Western Orthodox church that attempted to create a fully French-language, Western-rite Orthodox liturgical tradition under the canonical umbrella of Eastern Orthodoxy — eventually receiving canonical recognition from the Russian Orthodox Church Outside Russia (ROCOR) and later entering a complex period of jurisdictional dispute that ultimately led to the church's dissolution and its members dispersing to other Orthodox jurisdictions.

The ECOF's founding inspiration was the work of Fr. Denis (Eugene Fellippe) in the post-WWII period and developed under the leadership of Archbishop Jean (Kovalevsky), who developed a distinctive Western-rite Orthodox liturgy in French combining ancient Gallican and other Western liturgical traditions with Orthodox theology. The project represented an ambitious attempt to demonstrate that Orthodoxy was not culturally tied to Greek, Russian, or other Eastern national traditions but could have an authentic Western expression.

The ECOF ultimately foundered on jurisdictional disputes — the ambiguity of its canonical status, questions about the validity of its orders, and controversies about its bishops led to a fragmentation that left the church without clear canonical standing. Its dissolution was a significant setback for the Western Orthodox movement, though it produced liturgical resources and theological explorations that continue to influence Western Orthodox experiments. Many former ECOF members moved into the Antiochian Orthodox Church's Western Rite Vicariate.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Catholic Orthodox Church of France — an ambitious attempt to create French-language Western-rite Orthodox Christianity, ultimately dissolved through jurisdictional disputes — is historically significant as the most developed experiment in Western Orthodox liturgical tradition and a monument to the challenges of Orthodox canonical diversity.
